title: Short Stuff: Erfurt Latrine Disaster
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Erfurt Latrine Disaster, a supposed 1184 event in which the floor of a latrine-adjacent hall at the Petersburg Citadel in Erfurt collapsed during an assembly (hoftag) held by King Heinrich (Henry VI), sending nobles and attendees into a cesspool and killing dozens to hundreds by the hosts' estimate. The hosts cover medieval latrine design, castle waste chutes, the Château Gaillard siege of 1203, the survival of Heinrich, Ludwig and Conrad, Heinrich's later titles including overlord of England after holding Richard the Lionheart, and note that the story lacks a traceable primary source and may be a hoax.

segments.title: Opening and trigger warning
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Short Stuff episode and warn that the latrine disaster story is gross.

segments.title: 1184 dispute and Heinrich's assembly in Erfurt
segments.summary: A dispute between Ludwig II and Conrad of Wittelsbach leads King Heinrich VI, who was pushing for hereditary succession to the Holy Roman Empire, to convene a hoftag in Erfurt in July 1184.

segments.title: Petersburg Citadel and medieval latrine design
segments.summary: The assembly was held at the Petersburg Citadel, about fifteen years old. Hosts describe latrine alcoves placed beside banquet rooms so diners could leave the table without interrupting conversation.

segments.title: Medieval toilets, waste chutes and ammonia
segments.summary: Hosts describe wooden toilet seats over masonry basins, wiping with hay or moss, ammonia smells, and projecting latrines that dropped waste down castle walls.

segments.title: Sewage pipes and the Château Gaillard siege
segments.summary: Hosts note that some French castles used external waste pipes, which attackers climbed in a 1203 siege of Château Gaillard, and discuss how the climb worked.

segments.title: Cesspool beneath the Petersburg Citadel
segments.summary: Hosts say the Petersburg Citadel latrine emptied into a cesspool under the floor, cleaned about once a year, and that the hoftag hall sat above it.

segments.title: Floor collapse and deaths in the cesspool
segments.summary: The floor reportedly collapsed under the crowd of nobles and attendees, sending them into the cesspool; sixty to one hundred nobles' deaths are reported, with likely hundreds of total deaths from drowning and ammonia exposure.

segments.title: Survival of Heinrich, Conrad and Ludwig
segments.summary: All three major figures reportedly survived; Heinrich and Conrad were said to have stepped into an alcove off the collapsed floor, and Ludwig's survival is noted without detail.

segments.title: Heinrich's later titles and questionable sourcing
segments.summary: Hosts list Heinrich's later titles, including overlord of England after holding Richard the Lionheart hostage, then note the story has no traceable primary source and may be a hoax.

segments.title: Sign-off and iHeartRadio credit
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up the short episode and read the production credit.
